taskVersion.name: deadline-math-hard-direct
taskVersion.description: Exploratory hard set, answer-only mode. Convert deadlines to the reader's local time: relative dates, durations across a clock change, Unix and ISO timestamps, described dates, a traveling reader. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Six days from Saturday, October 24, 2026 is Friday, October 30, 2026. The deadline is 11:59 PM PT (Pacific Time) on that date.

On October 30, 2026, Pacific Time is PDT (UTC-7) since daylight saving time doesn't end until November 1, 2026. Madrid is on CET/CEST. On October 25, 2026, Europe switches from CEST (UTC+2) to CET (UTC+1). So on October 30, Madrid is UTC+1.

11:59 PM PDT = 23:59 UTC-7 = 06:59 UTC (next day) = 07:59 UTC+1 (next day).

So October 30, 23:59 PT → October 31, 07:59 Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

October 26, 2026: PT is UTC-7 (PDT, since it's before the first Sunday in November). 10:00 AM PT = 17:00 UTC on October 26.

72 hours later = 17:00 UTC on October 29, 2026.

Madrid (CET/CEST): On October 25, 2026, Europe switches from CEST (UTC+2) to CET (UTC+1) at 3:00 AM local time. So on October 29, Madrid is on CET = UTC+1.

17:00 UTC = 18:00 CET on October 29, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

First, let me determine when submissions close and when results are announced.

Submissions close: October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET (Eastern Time).

Results announced: exactly 36 hours later.

11:59 PM on October 31 + 36 hours = 11:59 AM on November 2, 2026 ET.

Now I need to determine what ET means and convert to Madrid time.

On November 2, 2026, the US falls back from EDT to EST. The fall back happens at 2:00 AM ET on November 1, 2026. Wait, let me check: US daylight saving time ends on the first Sunday of November in 2026. November 1, 2026 is a Sunday. So clocks fall back at 2:00 AM on November 1, 2026.

So October 31 at 11:59 PM — this is still EDT (UTC-4).

11:59 PM EDT on Oct 31 = 03:59 UTC on Nov 1.

Now add 36 hours: 03:59 UTC Nov 1 + 36 hours = 15:59 UTC Nov 2.

Madrid time on November 2, 2026: Europe's daylight saving time ends on the last Sunday of October. October 25, 2026 is the last Sunday of October. So by November 2, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).

15:59 UTC = 16:59 CET.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Let me convert Unix timestamp 1791788340 to a date.

1791788340 seconds from January 1, 1970 00:00:00 UTC.

1791788340 / 86400 = 20738.75 days approximately.

Let me work this out step by step:

- Years from 1970: 20738 days / 365.25 ≈ 56.78 years → around 2026-2027

Let me be more precise:
- From 1970 to 2026 = 56 years
- Days from 1970 to 2026: 56 × 365 + leap years
- Leap years between 1970-2025: 72,76,80,84,88,92,96,00,04,08,12,16,20,24 = 14 leap years
- Days = 56 × 365 + 14 = 20440 + 14 = 20454 days
- Remaining days: 20738.75 - 20454 = 284.75 days into 2026

Day 284 of 2026 (non-leap year):
- Jan: 31 (31)
- Feb: 28 (59)
- Mar: 31 (90)
- Apr: 30 (120)
- May: 31 (151)
- Jun: 30 (181)
- Jul: 31 (212)
- Aug: 31 (243)
- Sep: 30 (273)
- Oct: 11 → day 284

So October 11, 2026 in UTC, plus fractional day: 0.75 × 86400 = 64800 seconds = 18:00 UTC.

Wait, let me recompute more carefully.

20454 days × 86400 = 1,767,225,600 (Unix timestamp for Jan 1, 2026 00:00 UTC)

1791788340 - 1767225600 = 24,562,740 seconds into 2026

24,562,740 / 86400 = 284.291... days

Day 284 (0-indexed from day 0 = Jan 1): 
Actually day 0 = Jan 1, so day 284 = October 12 (let me recount).

Day 1-based counting:
284.291 days means we're in day 285 (1-indexed).
- Jan: 31, Feb: 28 (59), Mar: 31 (90), Apr: 30 (120), May: 31 (151), Jun: 30 (181), Jul: 31 (212), Aug: 31 (243), Sep: 30 (273), Oct: 285 - 273 = 12 → October 12

Fractional part: 0.291 × 86400 = 25,140 seconds = 6 hours, 59 minutes, 0 seconds → 06:59 UTC

Tokyo = UTC+9: 06:59 + 9:00 = 15:59

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 15:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid, Spain is in the CET/CEST time zone. October 25, 2026 is the day when clocks change from CEST (UTC+2) to CET (UTC+1). The change occurs at 3:00 AM local time (which is 01:00 UTC), so at 02:30 UTC on that date, the clocks have already fallen back and the local time is UTC+1.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I need to find the last Sunday of October 2026 and convert 11:59 PM Pacific Time to Madrid local time.

**Last Sunday of October 2026:**
October 2026: October 1 is a Thursday. Sundays in October: 4, 11, 18, 25. The last Sunday is October 25, 2026.

**Time zone considerations:**

On the last Sunday of October, Europe changes clocks. In 2026, Spain (CET/CEST) falls back on October 25. The clocks go back at 3:00 AM local time to 2:00 AM. So after that change, Spain is on CET (UTC+1).

For Pacific Time: US daylight saving ends on the first Sunday of November 2026 (November 1, 2026). So on October 25, the US is still on PDT (UTC-7).

So at 11:59 PM PDT on October 25, 2026:
- That's 23:59 UTC-7 = 06:59 UTC on October 26, 2026
- Spain is on CET (UTC+1) after the clock change: 06:59 + 1 = 07:59 on October 26, 2026

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In 2026, the US ends daylight saving time on Sunday, November 1, 2026. At that point, Eastern Time is still EDT (UTC-4) until 2:00 AM local time. 12:00 noon Eastern Time on that day would be EDT (UTC-4), since DST hasn't ended yet at noon (it ends at 2:00 AM the following morning... wait, let me reconsider).

US daylight saving time ends on the first Sunday in November. In 2026, that's November 1, 2026. At 2:00 AM EST (which is displayed as 2:00 AM), clocks "fall back" — meaning at 2:00 AM EDT, clocks go back to 1:00 AM EST. So DST ends at 2:00 AM local time on November 1, 2026. By noon on that day, the clocks have already fallen back, so noon would be EST (UTC-5).

Lima, Peru is on PET (UTC-5) year-round.

So 12:00 noon EST (UTC-5) = 12:00 noon PET (UTC-5).

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? Reply with exactly one line and nothing else: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney is AEDT (UTC+11) on October 5, 2026. New York is EDT (UTC-4) on that date.

5:00 PM Sydney (AEDT) = 17:00 - 11 = 06:00 UTC on October 5, 2026.

06:00 UTC - 4 hours = 02:00 EDT on October 5, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
